chunks: From him, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I love to persist upon the deed, even if it is little.'

key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: Ali ibn al-Husayn, the fourth Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on consistency versus quantity in good deeds?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) highlights the principle of *istiqamah* (steadfastness), teaching that consistent, small deeds are spiritually superior to occasional, large ones due to their sustainability and ease of maintenance. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the quality of persistence over the quantity of effort, ensuring that worship does not become a burden that leads to abandonment. The hadith serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate a lasting spiritual routine rather than seeking fleeting moments of intense devotion.

en.hubeali: From him, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> was saying: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> love to persists upon the (good) deed, and even though it may be little’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) would say, ‘I love to continue a good deed even if it is very little.’”
